blocks.text: Drop a stone into a still pond and rings spread outwards. A leaf floating on the surface bobs up and down but does not travel outwards with the ripples. That is the essential idea of a wave: energy moves through the medium, but the medium itself only vibrates about a fixed position.

blocks.title: Wave
blocks.text: A wave is a disturbance that transfers energy from one point to another through a medium (or through space, in the case of electromagnetic waves) without transferring the matter of the medium itself.

blocks.markdown:
### The quantities that describe a wave

- **Amplitude ($A$):** the maximum displacement of a particle from its rest position. It determines how much energy the wave carries — energy is proportional to the square of the amplitude.
- **Wavelength ($\lambda$):** the distance between two successive points in the same phase, for example crest to crest. Measured in metres.
- **Frequency ($f$):** the number of complete waves passing a point in one second. Measured in hertz (Hz), where $1\ \text{Hz} = 1\ \text{s}^{-1}$.
- **Period ($T$):** the time for one complete wave to pass a point. Measured in seconds.
- **Wavefront:** a line or surface joining all points that are in the same phase.

blocks.caption: Period and frequency are reciprocals of each other
The wave equation: speed = frequency × wavelength

blocks.markdown:
The wave equation follows directly from the definitions. In one period the wave advances exactly one wavelength, so

$$v = \frac{\lambda}{T} = \lambda \times \frac{1}{T} = f\lambda$$

There is nothing to memorise beyond that reasoning.

rows: No — a material medium is essential
Light, radio waves, water ripples, waves on a rope
Sound in air, ultrasound, compression waves in a spring

blocks.title: Using the wave equation
blocks.prompt: A vibrator produces water waves of frequency 50 Hz and wavelength 4.0 m. Calculate the speed of the waves.

steps.text: List the given quantities with their units.
Evaluate, noting that Hz × m gives m/s.

blocks.title: Finding a wavelength from period and speed
blocks.prompt: A wave of period 0.020 s travels through a medium at 300 m/s. Calculate its wavelength.

steps.text: Convert the period into a frequency.
Rearrange the wave equation for wavelength.
Substitute the speed and the frequency.
State the wavelength with its unit.
Shortcut: since v = λ/T, you can also write λ = vT = 300 × 0.020 = 6.0 m directly.

blocks.title: Frequency is set by the source
blocks.text: When a wave crosses from one medium into another, its FREQUENCY is unchanged because the source is still vibrating at the same rate. The speed changes because the new medium is different, so by v = fλ the wavelength must change too. This single fact explains refraction.

blocks.title: WAEC and JAMB tip
blocks.text: Watch out for questions that give the number of vibrations over an interval rather than a frequency. "300 complete vibrations in one minute" means f = 300 ÷ 60 = 5 Hz. Always reduce to vibrations per second before substituting.

points: A wave transfers energy without transferring matter.
Amplitude sets the energy carried; wavelength is the distance between successive points in phase.
Frequency is waves per second in hertz, and period is the reciprocal of frequency.
The wave equation v = fλ follows from the wave advancing one wavelength in one period.
Transverse waves vibrate perpendicular to their direction of travel; longitudinal waves such as sound vibrate along it and need a material medium.
